title: Dire à qui appartient quelque chose
summary: Choose possessive determiners by the thing possessed and distinguish de + owner from être à + owner.
objectives: Use mon/ton/son before a feminine vowel-initial noun.
Express possession with de and être à.

sections.title: The owner chooses the row; the possessed noun chooses the form
paragraphs: A possessive determiner replaces the article before a noun. For one owner: my = mon/ma/mes; your with tu = ton/ta/tes; his or her = son/sa/ses. Choose the masculine singular, feminine singular or plural form from the thing possessed, not the owner's gender. Son vélo can mean his bicycle or her bicycle because un vélo is masculine.

For plural owners: our = notre/nos; your with vous = votre/vos; their = leur/leurs. Notre, votre and leur are singular-thing forms for either gender; nos, vos and leurs are plural-thing forms. Polite singular vous also uses votre/vos. Before a feminine singular noun beginning with a vowel or silent h, use mon, ton or son instead of ma, ta or sa: mon amie. The noun is still feminine.
points: Do not add le or la before a possessive determiner.
One thing: mon/ma, ton/ta, son/sa, notre, votre, leur. Several things: mes, tes, ses, nos, vos, leurs.

examples.english: Lina is looking for her bicycle and her jacket.
examples.note: Un vélo (m.) and une veste (f.) determine son and sa.

examples.english: Paul is looking for his jacket.
examples.note: The owner's gender does not change sa.

examples.english: Here are my keys and your glasses.
examples.note: Plural nouns take mes/tes regardless of gender.

examples.english: My friend is arriving with her story.
examples.note: Une amie and une histoire remain feminine; the vowel/silent h triggers mon/son.

examples.english: Our house is near your apartment.
examples.note: Singular possessed nouns take notre/votre with either gender.

examples.english: Our neighbours are looking for their children.

examples.note: Leur is singular; context can mean a shared book or each child's own book.

mistakes.why: Use mon before a feminine noun starting with a vowel.

sections.title: De puts an owner after the thing
paragraphs: Use thing + de + owner: le sac de Lina means Lina's bag. French does not add an English possessive apostrophe-s. De contracts with a following definite le or les, but not with a personal name without an article: le sac du professeur, le sac de Lina. De becomes d' before a vowel.
points: Un sac (m.) = a bag. The thing comes before its owner in this pattern.

mistakes.why: Use the French de construction, not English apostrophe-s.

sections.title: Être à states who owns it
paragraphs: In a sentence, être à + a name or stressed pronoun means belong to: ce sac est à Lina, ce sac est à moi. Compare le sac de Lina (a noun phrase) with le sac est à Lina (a complete ownership statement). Use a stressed pronoun after à: moi, toi, lui, elle, nous, vous, eux, elles. Être agrees with the thing or things possessed.
points: À qui ? asks whose it is or who it belongs to.

examples.note: À takes the stressed pronoun moi.

mistakes.why: After à, use the stressed form moi.

practice.prompt: Lina owns a masculine livre. Supply her possessive: '___ livre'.
practice.explanation: The noun's masculine gender determines son.

practice.prompt: Say my before feminine amie: '___ amie'.
Rewrite 'Paul's bicycle' using le vélo and de.
practice.explanation: Put the thing before de + owner.

practice.prompt: Use the stressed pronoun meaning me: 'Ce livre est à ___.'
Use your for one familiar person before plural chaussures: '___ chaussures'.
Use our before singular feminine école: '___ école'.
practice.explanation: Notre is used for a singular thing of either gender.

practice.prompt: Use their before plural billets: '___ billets'.
Use their before one masculine appartement: '___ appartement'.
Address one customer politely. Supply your: '___ adresse, madame ?'
practice.explanation: Polite singular vous uses votre before a singular noun.

practice.prompt: Supply the ownership preposition: 'Ces sacs sont ___ nous.'
practice.explanation: Être à + owner expresses belong to.

practice.prompt: Does son in 'son vélo' prove that the owner is male?
practice.explanation: Son agrees with masculine vélo, not the owner's gender.

practice.prompt: Use our before plural amies: '___ amies'.
practice.explanation: The plural possessed noun takes nos.

practice.prompt: Use his before feminine histoire (silent h): '___ histoire'.
practice.explanation: Silent h triggers son instead of sa.

practice.prompt: Write the ownership statement using ces livres + être + à + eux in the present.
practice.explanation: Plural livres requires sont, and à takes stressed eux.

practice.prompt: Use your for several listeners before plural enfants: '___ enfants'.
practice.explanation: Vous has the plural-thing determiner vos.

production_task.prompt: Sort belongings after a class: identify your bag, a friend's keys and something belonging to the group. Use a possessive determiner, de and être à.
production_task.model_answer: Voici mon sac. Ce sont les clés de Nadia. Ces livres sont à nous.
production_task.translation: Here is my bag. These are Nadia's keys. These books belong to us.
rubric: Choose the determiner from the possessed noun.
Put a named owner after de.
Use à plus a stressed pronoun for the ownership statement.
